We have granted the underwriters an option for a period of 30 calendar days from the date of this prospectus supplement to purchase up to an additional 6,000,000 shares of our Class A Common Stock at a price of $622.91875 per share. If such option is exercised, we expect to enter into additional forward sale agreements with each of the forward purchasers in respect of the number of shares of our Class A Common Stock that are subject to the exercise of such option. Unless the context requires otherwise, the term “forward sale agreements” as used in this prospectus supplement includes any additional forward sale agreements that we may enter into with a forward purchaser in connection with the exercise by the underwriters of their option to purchase additional shares. If we enter into additional forward sale agreements, and if in the good faith, commercially reasonable judgment of a forward purchaser, it or its affiliate is unable to borrow, or is unable to borrow at a stock loan rate not greater than a specified rate, and deliver for sale on the anticipated closing date for the exercise of such option, a number of shares of our Class A Common Stock underlying its additional forward sale agreement, or if certain other conditions to such forward seller’s obligations have not been satisfied, then we will issue and sell directly to the underwriters a number of shares of our Class A Common Stock equal to the number of shares of our Class A Common Stock that such forward seller does not borrow and deliver. NVIDIA Corporation, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc., and Broadcom Inc. (collectively, the “Cornerstone Investors”) have, severally and not jointly, indicated an interest in purchasing up to an aggregate of $5.0 billion of shares of Class A common stock offered in this offering at the same price and on the same terms and conditions as the other purchasers in this offering. Because these indications of interest are not binding agreements or commitments to purchase, any of the Cornerstone Investors may determine to purchase more, fewer, or no shares of Class A common stock in this offering, or the underwriters may determine to sell more, fewer, or no shares of Class A common stock to any of the Cornerstone Investors. The underwriters will receive the same underwriting discount on any shares of Class A common stock purchased by the Cornerstone Investors as they will from the other shares of Class A common stock sold to the public in this offering. It is expected that delivery of the Class A Common Stock will be made against payment therefor on October 29, 2026, which is the second business day following the trade date for the Class A Common Stock (such settlement cycle being referred to as “T+2”). Under Rule 15c6-1 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), trades in the secondary market generally are required to settle in one business day, unless the parties to any such trade expressly agree otherwise. Accordingly, purchasers who wish to trade the Class A Common Stock prior to the business day preceding the settlement date will be required, by virtue of the fact that the Class A Common Stock initially will settle T+2, to specify an alternative settlement cycle at the time of any such trade to prevent a failed settlement. Purchasers of the Class A Common Stock who wish to trade the Class A Common Stock prior to the business day preceding the settlement date should consult their own advisors. Consequently, we anticipate there will be no dilutive effect on our earnings per share except during periods when the average market price of shares of our Class A Common Stock or Class C Common Stock, as applicable, is above the applicable adjusted forward sale price, which is initially $622.91875 per share, subject to increase or decrease based on the overnight bank funding rate, less a spread, and subject to decrease by amounts related to expected dividends on shares of our Class A Common Stock or Class C Common Stock, as applicable, during the term of the forward sale agreements and in connection with settlement involving shares of our Class C Common Stock. Furthermore, if we determine the effect of the forward sale agreements is dilutive, the numerator of diluted earnings per share will be adjusted to reverse the derivative gain or loss recognized during the period because diluted earnings per share will be calculated as if the contract were accounted for in equity, and not as a derivative, during the relevant period. Upon settlement of the forward sale agreements, delivery of shares of our Class A Common Stock or Class C Common Stock, as applicable, to the forward purchasers will result in dilution to our earnings per share. S-7 Table of Contents Conflicts of Interest All of the proceeds from the sale of shares of our Class A Common Stock offered by the forward sellers in this offering (excluding proceeds, if any, paid to us with respect to any shares of our Class A Common Stock that we may sell to the underwriters in lieu of the forward sellers selling such shares as further described elsewhere in this prospectus supplement) will be paid to the forward purchasers. Because Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC and Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC or their affiliates and/or agents, in their capacity as forward sellers, will receive more than 5% of the net proceeds of this offering, Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC and Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC are deemed to have a conflict of interest within the meaning of Rule 5121 of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. (“FINRA”). Accordingly, this offering will be conducted in compliance with the applicable provisions of FINRA Rule 5121. Pursuant to that rule, the appointment of a “qualified independent underwriter” is not required in connection with this offering, as the shares of our Class A Common Stock have a “bona fide public market” (as defined in FINRA Rule 5121). In addition, Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC and Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC may not make sales in this offering to any discretionary account without the prior written approval of the customer. See “Underwriting (Conflicts of Interest)” in this prospectus supplement for additional information. Risk Factors See “Risk Factors” in this prospectus supplement and the accompanying prospectus and other information incorporated by reference in this prospectus supplement and the accompanying prospectus for a discussion of some of the risks and other factors you should carefully consider before deciding to invest in shares of our Class A Common Stock. (1) The forward sellers have advised us that they intend to acquire shares of our Class A Common Stock to be sold in this offering through borrowings from third-party stock lenders. Subject to the occurrence of certain events, we will not be obligated to deliver shares under the forward sale agreements until later settlement of the forward sale agreements, which provide for settlement on a settlement date or dates to be specified at our discretion, subject to certain conditions, on or prior to November 19, 2027. The settlement of the forward sale agreements is also subject to acceleration by each forward purchaser upon the occurrence of S-8 Table of Contents certain events. See “Underwriting (Conflicts of Interest)—Forward Sale Agreements” in this prospectus supplement for a description of the forward sale agreements. (2) The number of shares of our Class A Common Stock outstanding immediately after this offering assumes full settlement of the forward sale agreements at the initial forward sale price of $622.91875 per share, without taking into account the Class C Effective Date. The number of shares of our Class A Common Stock to be outstanding immediately (i) before this offering, and (ii) after this offering, assuming full settlement of the forward sale agreements but without taking into account the Class C Effective Date, is, in each case, based on 2,214,455,318 shares of our Class A Common Stock outstanding as of September 30, 2026, and excludes any shares of our Class A Common Stock which may be issued under our equity compensation plans. FATCA withholding (if applicable) applies to dividends on our Class A Common Stock. While existing Treasury regulations would also require withholding on payments of gross proceeds of the sale or other disposition of our Class A Common Stock, the U.S. Treasury Department has indicated in subsequent proposed regulations its intent to eliminate this requirement. The U.S. Treasury Department has indicated that taxpayers may rely on these proposed regulations pending their finalization. You should consult your tax advisor regarding the effects of FATCA on your investment in our Class A Common Stock, including whether you would be eligible for a refund in the event that the 30% withholding under FATCA applies to a dividend on our Class A Common Stock.
